sentences.text:
....Respondents ORDER:
Heard the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent Nos.2 to 4.
2.

This Writ Petition is filed questioning the action of the respondents in trying to take possession of the property of the petitioner's company bearing D.No.10-1-45 without following the due process of law by issuing the impugned notices dated 04.10.2023 and 07.10.2023 and disconnecting water supply without giving proper opportunity of hearing to the petitioner.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the subject building was constructed much prior to 1985 and ever since the petitioner is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the same.

While so, the respondent No.3 addressed a letter, dated 07.08.2023 seeking consent for the purpose of acquisition of the petitioner's land to an extent of 983 Sq.yds affecting in 45mt wide Master Plan Road widening from Asilmetta Junction to Siripuram Junction (Dutt Island).
In the said letter, the respondent No.3 requested the petitioner to produce consent with relevant documents if any legal directions to process for issue of compensation and TDR as per rules.

sentences.text: In reply to the same the petitioner vide letter dated 22.08.2023 addressed to the respondent No.3 with a request to provide the documents mentioned in Para No.4 of the letter from Item Nos.1 to 11.

Then, the respondent No.3 addressed another letter to the petitioner dated 29.08.2023 informing that VMRDA has prepared a master plan to GVMC initiating 30 Master Plan Roads as per the procedure to facilitate the roads network to the public i.e. preparation of RDP and publication of the same in the daily news papers for calling objections/suggestions if any afterwards GVMC has brought to the notice of Executive Authority for approval as per due process.

For the property affecting in road widening the applicant is eligible for TDR @ ratio of 1:4 as per G.O.Ms.No.223,
M.A & U.D. Dept dated 09.07.2018 chapter- XII, Rule No.167(1) as per the said G.O.
5.

It was further informed in the said letter that in this process, the ITC premises property compound walls and open site bearing D.No.10-1-45 and 10-1-46, R37 are affecting in 45 mt & 20 mt wide Master Plan Road widening from Asilmetta Junction to Siripuram Junctions (Dutt Island)
nearly running length 111 mt, area 983 Sq.yds.

As per the sanctioned Master Plan alignment only,
the GVMC prepared RDP's for implementation.
Hence, the petitioner was requested the Branch Manager, ITC Group Ltd., to handover the affected portion to GVMC by way of consent and related documents.

Thereafter, the petitioner received notice under Section 635 Act, 1955 with respect to the subject property, dated 04.10.2023 to submit ownership documents and copy of the approved plan within 3 days from serving of this notice, otherwise it will be declared that there is no approval plan and accordingly necessary lawful action will be taken.
6. The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner submits that the said impugned notice dated 04.10.2023 was served on 07.10.2023 at 11:00 A.M.

Immediately, the respondent No.3 issued the final impugned notice dated 07.10.2023 for the subject building unauthorizedly contrary to the provisions of HMC Act and Bye-Laws made there under as if there is no information furnished by the petitioner and the petitioner did not show any cause within the stipulated time.

In the earlier notice also the said construction of the building was treated as un-authorized construction and unless the petitioner appears within 3 days before the respondent No.3 and submit the above said required documents the structure will be pulled down within 3 days by following the due process with the expenses of the petitioner as per Section 596/Section 461 (4)/Section 461-A of HMC Act.
7.

On the other hand, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the respondent Nos.2 to 4 submits that the petitioner has not produced any relevant documents for the subject building pursuant to the impugned notice dated 04.10.2023 and as such the respondent No.3 has issued final notice dated 07.10.2023, in the matter of acquisition of the Rehabilitation of the subject building for the purpose of road widening and the due process will be followed.
8.

In view of the above said facts and circumstances, since there was no much time gap between the notices dated 04.10.2023 and 07.10.2023, it cannot be treated as sufficient time given to the petitioner to submit the necessary documents in support of petitioner's claim and as such the petitioner is permitted to submit its explanation pursuant to the impugned notices dated 04.10.2023 and 07.10.2023 within a period of two (02) weeks from the date of receipt of this order by enclosing all the necessary documents in support of the petitioner's claim.

On receipt of the same,
the respondent No.3 shall proceed with the enquiry pursuant to the above said notice and upon Itc Limited vs Gov Of Ap on 11 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92895747/
2 hearing of all the parties concerned including the petitioner and upon verification of the records and the subject property an appropriate final decision shall be taken by the respondent-authorities strictly in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of eight (08)
weeks thereafter.

sentences.text: Till such time there shall be an order of status-quo to be maintained with respect to the subject building during the enquiry under the above said impugned notices.
However, it does not preclude for the respondents to proceed in accordance with law for the purpose of acquisition of the subject building.
The existing water supply to the subject building if any shall not be disconnected pending the above said enquiry if the petitioner is otherwise entitled and not a defaulter.
9. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.
As a sequel, Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.

Interim orders, if any,
stands vacated.
